newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK LODENICE SHELVES CAPITAL INCREASE.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK LODENICE SHELVES CAPITAL INCREASE.

text.p: Slovak shipbuilder, Slovenske Lodenice a.s. (SLK) on Thursday said it will not increase its basic capital through a share issue, saying it could not meet a planned November 30 deadline for the issue.
"It was impossible to fulfill the conclusions of the shareholders meeting (by November 30), mainly due to prolonged negotiations with the finance ministry," said Ladislav Zvolensky of SLK.
SLK shareholders last May approved the issue which would increase the firm's basic capital by 170 million crowns to just under 800 million crowns.
Shareholders approved the issue of 173,694 new shares with a nominal value of 1,000 crowns in three tranches.
The finance ministry officials who were to have approved the plan were not immediately available for comment.
Another SLK official, however, hinted the plan may have also failed due to a lack of interest in the issue from the company's new owners.
"There were a lot of changes in the company since May and it seems that the new owners have not stuck to the plan," the official, who did not wish to be named, told Reuters.
Slovak medical supplier Chirana Prema and its daughter Chirana Import-Export took three of nine seats on the supervisory board of SLK in August.
The firm's stake in Slovenske Lodenice, the nation's sole shipbuilder, has not been made public, but an official for the shipbuilder said it controlled "over 16 percent".
Zvolensky said the company planned an extraordinary shareholders meeting for December 23, adding that the situation of the unsuccessful capital increase was so far not on the agenda.
"But we expect this meeting to approve a bond issue, as it is also a way how to raise funds," he said.
Further details of the bond issue were not available.
Lodenice, building 15 to 17 river and maritime cargo vessels annually, ranks among the country's largest exporters.
